What started as a laundry problem turned into a startup with 70+ successful pilots.

Meet Pratham, the student founder behind Dhobi, a laundry-tech startup making laundry pickup and delivery faster and more convenient.

From spotting a gap in everyday convenience to testing the idea with 3-4 star hotels across Bengaluru, Pratham has taken Dhobi from an idea to real-world pilots.

The biggest milestone? Making it to the top 500 out of 26,000+ applicants for Gautam Adani’s out Vande Bharatam initiative.

And he’s only getting started.

For Pratham, building beyond the syllabus means having the courage to start before you have everything figured out. And that’s exactly what he’s doing.

What if Al could help catch cancer before it’s too late? 🧬 

Two Polaris students, Shivadharushni M and Chandan KT, are working with a team at California State University, Fullerton, to explore exactly that.

Their research focuses on training Al to detect skin lesions, with a particular focus on catching melanoma rather than overlooking it.

But in healthcare, getting the answer right isn’t enough. Knowing when the Al isn’t sure matters just as much.

A fascinating look at how student research, international collaboration, and Al are coming together to explore a problem that could make a real difference.

Think you can always spot a scammer? Well, think again 

Meet SmartInbox, built by a Polaris student Soham Pal to help you spot suspicious SMS messages before they catch you off guard.

From checking a single text to classifying entire batches of messages, SmartInbox uses machine learning to flag potential spam, estimate how risky a message is, and track spam patterns through analytics. It even lets admins retrain the model as new patterns emerge.

Because in a world where scam messages can look completely legit, spotting the red flags matters...

author: polariscampus
text:
What if places could talk? 🎧

That’s the idea behind Loci, built by Polaris students Sakshi Kasat and Manav Nayak.

Inspired by a boat ride in the Netherlands, they set out to make exploring the world more immersive - letting places tell their stories without you having to look them up.

But there was a catch: how do you know exactly where someone is, especially indoors? From exploring Wi-Fi fingerprinting to motion sensors and spatial mapping, the team had to tackle a real engineering challenge.

And the best part? When technology isn’t sure, Loci is designed not to guess.

One memory. One idea. Two student builders.
